newsitem.title: GERMANY: German confectionery sector strike blocks industry.
newsitem.headline: German confectionery sector strike blocks industry.

text.p: Processing schedules in the German confectionery industry were disrupted by a burst strike action on Monday, industry sources said.
So far the strikes have been selective and allowed plants to plan ahead and rejig supply and output flows.

On Monday, the action was widened to 12,000 out of 58,000 workers in the confectionery sector. Last week, 4,700 workers went on strike in seven key plants at four companies in a bid to maintain full sick and holiday payments.

"Key plants are now hit by the trouble and if it carries on, it could hamper new ordering and block transport of goods to shops," said Karsten Keunecke, managing director of confectionery industry association BDS in Bonn.
The relevant union NGG in Hamburg said talks with employers on Friday over sick and holiday pay in new 1997 wage packages were fruitless.
Keunecke said stores' supplies of seasonal chocolate specialities could be threatened if the action intensified.
Cocoa traders said orders for beans and butter for 1997 and 1998 dates, which had recently weakened due to sterling and futures strength, were not yet affected.
"If production stops at major plants, then their raw materials ordering is also paralysed," Keunecke said, adding "Small and medium sized plants seem to be faring better."
It was unclear whether the strike might be resolved soon.
BDS chairman Klaus Schuetze told German radio on Monday consumers should start hoarding Christmas seasonal products. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
